pageCache.pageTitle: Vision and Values - The Bethlem and Maudsley Hospital School
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
At Maudsley and Bethlem Hospital School, part of The Goldfinch Trust, we work together to provide Exceptional Educational Experiences for children and young people with mental and physical health needs. Our vision is for every child and young person, with their individual needs, to thrive as a curious learner. Our mission, vision and values provide a shared framework for how we work across the Trust and reflect the principles agreed following consultation across our three settings.
Mission Vision Values Document
Our Mission
We exist to work together to provide Exceptional Educational Experiences for children and young people with mental and physical health needs. We deliver an ambitious, creative and agile curriculum underpinned by care, meeting every pupil where they are to ensure meaningful impact.
Working together is fundamental to this mission. Our approach brings together learners, families, staff, clinicians and other professionals, recognising the importance of strong partnerships around each child and young person.
Our curriculum is ambitious, creative and agile because our learners have individual needs and circumstances. Meeting every pupil where they are means responding to those needs with care while maintaining high expectations and focusing on meaningful educational impact.
Our Vision
Our vision is for every child and young person, with their individual needs, to thrive as a curious learner.
We recognise that every learner is different. Our approach starts with the individual, their needs and their potential. We aim to create educational experiences that support curiosity, recognise achievement in all its forms and enable learners to thrive.
Our vision is supported by an approach that combines ambition with care. We maintain high expectations, adapt and find solutions where needed, and work in partnership with the people around each learner. Together, these principles shape how we support children and young people across the Trust.
Our values
Our values inform our decision making, shape our culture and define how we work day to day:
These values run through how we work across the Trust, including our strategy, curriculum, leadership and decision making. They provide a shared foundation for how we support learners, work with families and professionals, and develop our schools.
Sustainability is embedded throughout our work rather than standing as a separate value. It applies across strategy, curriculum, estates, procurement and decision making, ensuring it remains a visible and practical part of how the Trust develops over time.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Frankie the Robot - News Blog - The Bethlem and Maudsley Hospital School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Frankie the Robot
The school has recently acquired a Nao interactive humanoid robot, which we have named Frankie.
A Nao is a small humanoid robot designed to interact with people. It's packed with sensors (and character) and it can walk, dance, speak, and recognise faces and objects. Now in its sixth generation, it is used in research, education, and healthcare all over the world.
Frankie will be making an appearance in lessons, and we hope that they will be used for developing coding and programming skills in Computing and ICT, and that they will also be able to play a role in other subject areas, where they can interact with students, and help make learning more interesting and fun.
At present we are still getting to know Frankie discovering and developing the things that they can do, and we hope to have more updates in the future.
You can find out more about Nao robots here https://www.softbankrobotics.com/emea/en/nao

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Chair of Governors - The Bethlem and Maudsley Hospital School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Chair of Governors
Dear Parent or Carer,
On behalf of the local governors and staff of Maudsley and Bethlem Hospital School (MBHS) and, since September 2025 King's College Hospital School, (KCHS), welcome. Ofsted has judged MBHS to be ‘Outstanding’ in all inspections since 2008 and we are very proud of our highly skilled and dedicated staff. We are also delighted now to include KCHS within our provision. As far as we can, we aim to be an ordinary school for exceptional children and young people in extraordinary circumstances. We appreciate that our pupils are with us because they are currently unwell, but this is all the more reason why we are committed to providing them with the most engaging and relevant curriculum possible, for every day that we have the privilege of working with them. We maintain the highest expectations of and for our pupils and work, in conjunction with their medical and other professional teams, to ensure their attendance and commitment to their education. The vast majority of our pupils leave us to re-join their own 'home' school; some are with us only a few days, some weeks and some for a number of months. We work closely with our pupils' 'home' school, to ensure that their learning is personalised to their need, their stage of learning and their circumstances. Where appropriate, we also ensure that pupils can work together during some of their learning.
Despite the seriousness of our purpose, you will find us as any school should be; stimulating, challenging and full of fun.
Welcome to our school.
Rebecca Osuntokun, Chair of Local Governors

Our mission, vision and values provide a shared framework for how we work across the Trust and reflect the principles agreed following consultation across our three settings.
Mission Vision Values Document
Our Mission
We exist to work together to provide Exceptional Educational Experiences for children and young people with mental and physical health needs. We deliver an ambitious, creative and agile curriculum underpinned by care, meeting every pupil where they are to ensure meaningful impact.
Working together is fundamental to this mission. Our approach brings together learners, families, staff, clinicians and other professionals, recognising the importance of strong partnerships around each child and young person.
Our curriculum is ambitious, creative and agile because our learners have individual needs and circumstances. Meeting every pupil where they are means responding to those needs with care while maintaining high expectations and focusing on meaningful educational impact.
Our Vision
Our vision is for every child and young person, with their individual needs, to thrive as a curious learner.
We recognise that every learner is different. Our approach starts with the individual, their needs and their potential. We aim to create educational experiences that support curiosity, recognise achievement in all its forms and enable learners to thrive.
Our vision is supported by an approach that combines ambition with care. We maintain high expectations, adapt and find solutions where needed, and work in partnership with the people around each learner. Together, these principles shape how we support children and young people across the Trust.
Our values
Our values inform our decision making, shape our culture and define how we work day to day:
These values run through how we work across the Trust, including our strategy, curriculum, leadership and decision making. They provide a shared foundation for how we support learners, work with families and professionals, and develop our schools.
Sustainability is embedded throughout our work rather than standing as a separate value. It applies across strategy, curriculum, estates, procurement and decision making, ensuring it remains a visible and practical part of how the Trust develops over time.

About Us
Welcome to Maudsley and Bethlem Hospital School. We hope this website will give you some idea of the education we provide whilst you are in hospital.
Our Mission Statement:
To create a safe and inclusive learning environment for young people to enjoy, achieve and move forward with their lives.
Welcome from the HeadteacherWelcome from the Chair of Governors
What are our aims?
Our Values
The statements below describe how we choose to work together, the team culture we value, and how we look to get things done.
Ambitious. We are ambitious for our students’ learning. We plan to be a turning point in their lives.
Collaborative. Our success depends on collaboration and our ability to work as a team.
Steadfast. We confront calmly the stigma and prejudice that still surrounds mental health. We can change attitudes in society, through our work.
Kind. We are kind and compassionate even when we need to have difficult conversations.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from Maudsley and Bethlem Hospital School - The Bethlem and Maudsley Hospital School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from Maudsley and Bethlem Hospital School
Dear Parent or Carer,
Welcome to our website where you can find out more about our outstanding school. I am incredibly proud of the students and staff here at Maudsley and Bethlem Hospital School. Our school embodies our core values of ambition, collaboration, steadfastness, and kindness. We are dedicated to providing the best possible education for our learners.
While no one chooses to be in hospital, we strive to keep our students connected to their educational journeys from the moment they arrive until the reintegration process begins. Our students continually demonstrate their ambition and desire to achieve, despite their circumstances. We are committed to mirroring their ambition and going the extra mile to help them stay engaged with learning.
At Maudsley and Bethlem Hospital School, we offer a personalised curriculum tailored to each student's unique needs through our Learning Pathways. This approach ensures that we map out each student's curriculum intent, providing a broad and balanced curriculum that encompasses academic excellence, personal development, and career readiness. We also prioritise enhancing our students' access to cultural capital opportunities, enriching their educational experience.
Additionally, we are an exam centre, and if your child is with us during an exam season, they will have the opportunity to sit their exams in a calm and supportive environment.
I am also proud to announce that our school has been awarded the RACE Charter Mark. One aspect of this is recognition of our commitment to a diverse and inclusive curriculum. Our updated Curriculum Policy ensures pupils receive an education that reflects the UK's rich and varied history, along with the diverse heritages of our students. We are dedicated to including marginalised sources of knowledge, representing a range of global and historical perspectives, and aligning our learning content with global frameworks.
We will allocate a Key Teacher to your child who will be your main contact point with the school, but all of our highly experienced staff will support your child during their time with us. We will work closely with home schools, the local authority, our hospital partners, and, of course, you.
Please do not hesitate to contact us if you have any questions about your child's education while they are attending our school.
Maarten Crommelin, CEO / Accounting Officer / Headteacher
The Goldfinch Trust / Maudsley and Bethlem Hospital School

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Frankie the Robot - News Blog - The Bethlem and Maudsley Hospital School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Frankie the Robot
The school has recently acquired a Nao interactive humanoid robot, which we have named Frankie.
A Nao is a small humanoid robot designed to interact with people. It's packed with sensors (and character) and it can walk, dance, speak, and recognise faces and objects. Now in its sixth generation, it is used in research, education, and healthcare all over the world.
Frankie will be making an appearance in lessons, and we hope that they will be used for developing coding and programming skills in Computing and ICT, and that they will also be able to play a role in other subject areas, where they can interact with students, and help make learning more interesting and fun.
At present we are still getting to know Frankie discovering and developing the things that they can do, and we hope to have more updates in the future.
You can find out more about Nao robots here https://www.softbankrobotics.com/emea/en/nao

pageCache.pageTitle: The Pears Maudsley Centre Update - News Blog - The Bethlem and Maudsley Hospital School
pageCache.text:
The Pears Maudsley Centre Update
The Maudsley and Bethlem Hospital school provides highly personalised, specialist education for pupils whilst they are receiving care for a range of mental health and psychiatric conditions.
Our Senior Philanthropy Manager, Seren Bradshaw, recently visited the school and, as key supporters of the school, we wanted to share this report with you.
The Pears Maudsley Centre Update Report
Outstanding education at a challenging time
No child chooses to be in hospital. At a time when you desperately want to fit in, it can be a disruptive and unfamiliar experience. That’s why the Maudsley and Bethlem Hospital School works hard to keep pupils connected to their educational journeys from the moment they arrive.
Rated as Outstanding by OFTSED, the school provides tailored education to children and young people aged 4 -18, who are inpatients or outpatients at the Bethlem Royal Hospital in Kent, or the Maudsley Hospital. The staff are dedicated to giving pupils the best possible individual learning experiences, and support in returning to mainstream school or onto work or apprenticeships.
Moving the school’s Maudsley site over to the Pears Maudsley Centre will offer a truly exceptional physical environment and educational provision that will now match the schools outstanding OFSTED rating. Providing students with significantly improved facilities will no doubt improve their overall learning experience and in turn educational outcomes.

Our wonderful teacher Jen Carney was recognised for her impact at the Educators Trust Awards 2024 on Friday 19th April.
This was quite a memorable event! A highly formal occasion in the 14th Century Merchant Taylor’s Hall (https://www.merchant-taylors.co.uk/) , the awards recognised teachers and educators from across society and Jen was in esteemed company. There were only 13 winners and we were very proud to hear Jen’s achievements read out to the packed chamber.
Jen was nominated for her outstanding adaptability and creativity in responding to the needs of the pupils and her impact on the school as a whole. Well done Jen and we hope you had a night to remember!

pageCache.pageTitle: Secondary Citizenship Teacher of the Year - News Blog - The Bethlem and Maudsley Hospital School
pageCache.text:
Secondary Citizenship Teacher of the Year
We are delighted to announce that on 9th June 2025 our wonderful teacher Anthony Gunning was officially recognised and awarded the prestigious title of Secondary Citizenship Teacher of the Year. This award was presented to Anthony by Rt. Hon. Lord Norton of Louth.
This national accolade celebrates Anthony’s exceptional work in promoting Citizenship as a vital subject and his inspiring efforts to foster democratic culture and active citizenship among young people. The award citation highlighted his contributions as “a leading example for teachers and schools across the country.”
Anthony’s dedication to enriching students’ understanding of civic responsibility and democratic engagement stands as a beacon of excellence in education. His work not only elevates the subject of Citizenship but also empowers the next generation to become thoughtful, engaged members of society.
This is a significant achievement, and we are incredibly proud to see his commitment and passion recognised on a national stage.
Congratulations, Anthony!
